steps.text: Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat until almost smoking. Cook and stir the eggplant cubes until they begin to brown, 3 to 5 minutes. Remove the eggplant with a slotted spoon, and set aside.

Heat 2 more tablespoons of oil in the skillet over medium-high heat, and cook and stir the onions just until they begin to soften, about 30 seconds. Stir in the garlic, and cook and stir an additional 30 seconds. Mix in the soy sauce, water, oyster sauce, chili garlic sauce, sugar, and black pepper, and stir to form a smooth sauce. Return the eggplant to the skillet, lower the heat, and allow the vegetables and sauce to simmer until the eggplant is tender and almost all the liquid has been absorbed, about 5 minutes. Drizzle sesame oil over the dish, and give one final brief stir to combine.

raw_recipe.headline: Spicy Eggplant
raw_recipe.description: Eggplant cubes are stir-fried until browned, then simmered in a spicy Asian-inspired sauce with onion and garlic until meltingly tender.

review.reviewBody: When I originally posted this recepie it called for Thai chili garlic paste (or chili bean sauce) depending on what you can find. In China I use spicey black bean sauce, and in the U.S. the Thai paste. Depends on what I have availiable. I'm not sure why it would ever be too liquid, as I more often have to add extra water rather than thicken it. I love this recepie and it is a staple in our household. Fast easy & healthy. Just the way I like them ^_^

This was really good! To cut down on the fat, I used olive oil spray to sauté the eggplant and onions. I also used 1 tsp of the chili paste, as 1 tbsp would have been way too spicy for me. I added cubed Trader Joe's baked siracha tofu and served the mixture over zucchini noodles. Filling and flavorful!

The wife loved it! I used peanut oil on the eggplant and made sure that they browned really well (longer than 3-5), and used sesame seed oil to sauté the onion and garlic. To top it off, I dusted the combined eggplant and spices with cumin (because I really wanted to make Szechuan cumin pork eggplant). Giving it 4 stars because cooking times not accurate.

I have an abundance of Japanese Eggplants from my garden and have been looking for different things to do with them. I do a lot of Chinese cooking and recalled a recipe similar to this that I did years ago. Looking this recipe over, it seemed very authentic. And it is. The flavors blend beautifully. Not too spicy. Just right for me. I did add about 2 lbs of thinly sliced pork loin, which I marinated for 30 minutes in a mixture of soy sauce, rice wine, and cornstarch. I also tripled the sauce. I stir fried the vegetables, removed them from the pan, and then stir fried my pork separately. When the pork was cooked, I added the veggies back to the pan and added the sauce. Beautiful one dish meal that I will definitely be repeating. Thanks for a great recipe!

Well this was simply fantastic...AND I messed it up. I diced up some raw chicken thighs and had everything prepped and ready to plop into my cast iron skillet. Oops, I started the onions first. When I realized my mistake I just tossed everything into the skillet and holy cow, it was amazing. I can only imagine how much better it will be when I follow the steps properly.

I have made this several times. My family can't get enough of it. We used to get this in a Chinese Restaurant, but moved away from that city. Every family get-together, they request this dish. The only thing that makes it better (the same as the restaurant), is that I cook 3 large sausages (taken out of the casings)- cooked separately, then added to the Spicy Eggplant dish when it's all completed. The sausage meat that I buy is mild, since the eggplant dish is spicy. With the sausage meat, just keep chopping it up with a wooden spoon until it's in small pieces. Add to the Eggplant dish at the end. So yummy.

I love this recipe!!! I modify it a bit every time depending on what Ingredients I have on hand. I omit the sugar and instead of oyster sauce, I use a dash of fish sauce and add a table spoon of rice cooking wine. I add some of the minced garlic into the sauce as well as sauté some of it (about 1/3 in sauce.) I use a tbsp of Sambal Oelek chili paste and about a tsp of sriracha sauce. I chop the onion smallish instead of leaving it sliced, I think it goes better that way with the texture. I also cook the eggplant for about 8-10 minutes first before removing it from pan to cook the onion etc. Super easy recipe and easy to customize to your liking, I make it all the time!

Delicious recipe for spicy eggplant. My additions: I started with a mix of oils: canola, sesame oil, and a hot chili oil from my favorite Szechuan restaurant. I added a mix of minced garlic, ginger and scallion to the eggplant; cooked for a bit longer than 5 minutes; after removing the stir-fried eggplant, I added a bit more garlic-ginger-scallion to 1 tbl. Canola oil and added in 3 veggies: 1/2 chopped green pepper, I can sliced water chestnuts for great crunch, and scallion greens. Then I added the sauce, as written, with a touch more of sesame oil and a splash of rice vinegar. Served over brown rice.

This is so good! I wanted a quick recipe to use up all my eggplant and this one does not disappoint. I followed the recipe except for the oyster sauce, only because I did not want to run out and get some. I substituted Worchester sauce instead of the oyster sauce as someone suggested and it came out super tasty; I didn’t miss the oyster sauce at all. I added chili flakes at the end. This was a huge hit in my family. The second time I made it I added mushrooms and it also tasted great.

I just didn't add the onion, but this was delicious! I like a little more heat so I added some crushed red pepper flakes; maybe some Siracha would have worked well here, too. Added a splash of rice wine vinegar. I like a dish like this to be more mushy, so I cooked it about twice the amount of time. Very good recipe!

I’ve made this recipe many times with modifications. I caramelize the onions so they are soft and sweet. I make only a half recipe of the sauce, which is plenty for 4 small or 2 med-large Japanese eggplants. And to finish, after drizzling the sesame oil, I top with sesame seeds.
I use cooked chicken with this and one half chili garlic sauce for less spiciness and more fresh garlic and tiny bit of hoisin sauce.
Added sliced sweet peppers and jalapeno to the onions, and corn starch and rice wine to the sauce mixture. Garnished over jasmine rice with cilantro and toasted sesame. Sit down delicious!

Excellent recipe! I made this with some Thai eggplant fresh from the asian market and a smallish Chinese eggplant, added some fried tofu at the end and it was amazing! Tastes just like in the restaurant.
Great recipe! Salted and rinsed my eggplant before I cooked and added some rice wine vinegar. Will definitely make again!
I really liked this, but next time I will add more spice and some chives for color. I served with basmati rice, garlic shrimp and Japanese cucumbers in rice wine vinegar.
Delicious! Used sriracha sauce and eggplant I had frozen from my garden 8 months ago! Too bad most of the family doesn't like eggplant, more for my daughter and I!

My husband & I both liked it a lot---2nd day even better than first. After I finished it I cut the cubes into smaller pieces & added just a bit of water. Used siracha sauce since what I had was fresh. Served it over brown rice & with sliced raw veggies.

I did not add the sugar, and it does not need this! I used red onions as that is what I had in the house. I did not have the sesame oil and used olive oil. I did at 1 TBS ginger paste. It came out delicious!
Excellent recipe! Family loves it
